title: Buying options: the other side of the trade
summary: What a buyer pays and needs to win, why most bought options expire worthless, when a buy makes sense, and the app's rules for buying.

questions.q: You buy a call for ₹5. What is the most you can lose?
questions.why: A buyer's loss is capped at the premium paid.

questions.q: You buy the 1,100 call for ₹10. At expiry, where must the stock be for you to make money?
questions.why: You need the price past strike + premium: 1,100 + 10 = 1,110.

questions.q: How does time decay affect an option buyer?
options: It costs them a little every day
questions.why: The time value the seller collects is the buyer's daily cost.

questions.q: A delta 0.10 option ends in the money roughly:
questions.why: Delta roughly reads as the chance of finishing in the money: about 1 in 10.

questions.q: From Level 6, a bought leg with no sold leg to protect closes when:
options: It has lost half of what you paid
questions.why: The 50% stop keeps one bad bet from draining the account.
